blocks.text: INTRODUCTION
Purpose

These Terms and Conditions (the Terms) set out the legal framework under which Zatics Intelligence supplies Services, Software and Systems to its business clients, and the rights and responsibilities of each party in that relationship.

The Terms are intended to make the commercial relationship clear before work begins, to define how Scope, Fees, timelines, ownership, data and risk are managed, and to provide an orderly process for changes, approvals, payment and dispute resolution.
The Services are supplied to organizations for business purposes. They are not supplied to individuals acting as consumers.
Acceptance of Terms
The Client accepts these Terms by doing any of the following:
(a)	signing an Agreement that incorporates or refers to these Terms;
(b)	approving a Proposal, Blueprint or Change Order through the Client Portal, by email or by another electronic means, where that document refers to these Terms;
(c)	issuing a purchase order that Zatics Intelligence accepts in writing; or
(d)	authorizing the commencement of Services or accessing or using any Software, System or Client Portal supplied by Zatics Intelligence.
The individual who accepts these Terms on behalf of the Client confirms that he or she has authority to bind the Client.

Terms contained in a purchase order, vendor onboarding form, procurement policy or other document issued by the Client do not apply to the Services unless Zatics Intelligence expressly accepts them in a written document signed by an authorized representative of Zatics Intelligence.
When These Terms Become Binding
These Terms become binding on the Client and Zatics Intelligence on the earliest of the events described in the preceding Section 1.2.

A discussion, presentation, estimate or Proposal does not by itself create an obligation on Zatics Intelligence to perform a Project or on the Client to purchase Services. Zatics Intelligence is not required to begin a Project until an Agreement has been executed, the Blueprint has been approved where applicable, and any Upfront Fee that the Agreement makes a condition of commencement has been received.
A Proposal remains open for acceptance for the period stated in it or, if no period is stated, for thirty (30) calendar days from its date of issue.
Relationship Between These Terms and Individual Agreements

These Terms form the general framework for the relationship. Each engagement is documented in an Agreement that records the commercial particulars of that engagement, including the identity of the Client, the Fees, the Subscription Term and the Scope.

Where the Client has more than one Project or License, these Terms apply to each of them separately. An Agreement may take the form of a master agreement supported by separate order forms, statements of work or license schedules.

An Agreement may modify a provision of these Terms only if it identifies the Section being modified and states the modification expressly. A general statement that the Agreement prevails does not displace any Section of these Terms that is not identified.
Effective Date

These Terms take effect on the Terms Effective Date. As between Zatics Intelligence and a particular Client, the version of these Terms in force on the Effective Date of the Agreement governs that Agreement for its duration, subject to Section 1.6.
Updates to These Terms

Zatics Intelligence may update these Terms from time to time. An updated version will be published on the Client Portal or the official website, and Zatics Intelligence will notify the Client by email at least thirty (30) days before the updated version takes effect.

An updated version applies to Agreements entered into on or after its effective date and to any renewal of a Subscription Term that begins on or after that date. It does not apply to a Project or Subscription Term already in progress under an existing Agreement unless:
(a)	the Client agrees to it in writing;
(b)	the change is required by Applicable Law, an order of a competent authority, or a mandatory requirement of a Third Party Service provider;
(c)	the change is necessary to address a security risk; or
(d)	the change does not materially reduce the Client's rights or materially increase the Client's obligations.
Zatics Intelligence will maintain a record of each version in Section 39 and will provide earlier versions to the Client on request.
Order of Precedence
The documents that make up the contractual relationship rank in the following order. If there is a conflict between two documents, the document ranked higher prevails to the extent of the conflict.

Presentations, marketing materials, emails, meeting discussions and informal messages are not part of the Scope unless their content is recorded in the Agreement, the Approved Blueprint or a Change Order.
DEFINITIONS
Defined Terms
In these Terms, the following capitalized terms have the meanings given below. Each defined term is used with the same meaning throughout these Terms and in every document that incorporates them.
Acceptance means acceptance of a Blueprint, Deliverable or Milestone in accordance with Section 6 or Section 13, including deemed acceptance under Section 13.
Acceptance Criteria means the objective and testable conditions, stated in the Approved Blueprint or the Agreement, against which a Deliverable is assessed.

Agreement means the signed written commercial agreement, order form, statement of work or license schedule between Zatics Intelligence and the Client for the supply of Services, Systems or Licenses, together with the documents that rank within the order of precedence in Section 1.7.
AI Agent means an AI System configured to receive objectives or inputs, plan or sequence steps, and perform tasks or invoke tools or Third Party Services within a Configured Scope.
AI System means a System or component of a System that uses machine learning, large language models or other statistical or generative techniques to produce Outputs.
Applicable Law means the laws, regulations, binding regulatory requirements and orders of courts or authorities that apply to a party, to the Services or to a System in the relevant jurisdiction.

Authorized User means an individual whom the Client authorizes, in accordance with the Agreement, to access or use a System, an Existing Zatics Solution or the Client Portal on the Client's behalf, being an employee or contractor of the Client or another person permitted by the Agreement.
Autonomous System means a System, which may comprise one or more AI Agents, that carries out tasks, workflows or actions without requiring human instruction at each step, within its Configured Scope.

Blueprint means the written project document prepared by Zatics Intelligence that records the requirements, architecture, features, integrations, workflows, Deliverables, Milestones, dependencies, Acceptance Criteria, timeline and price of a Project. Approved Blueprint means the Blueprint in the version approved by the Client under Section 6, as updated by any Change Order.
Business Day means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday observed in India at the location from which Zatics Intelligence administers the relevant Agreement.
Change Order means a written document, approved by both parties in accordance with Section 9, that records a change to the Scope, the Fees, the timeline or other terms of an Agreement.
Change Request means a request by the Client, made in accordance with Section 9, to change the Scope, a Deliverable, the Approved Blueprint or the timeline.
Client means the organization identified as the client or licensee in the Agreement.

Client Content means documents, text, images, brand assets, specifications, templates and other materials, other than Client Data, that are supplied by or on behalf of the Client for use in a Project or a System.

Client Data means data, records, datasets and information, including Personal Data, that are supplied by or on behalf of the Client, collected by a System on the Client's behalf, or generated by a System from the processing of such data, and excludes Zatics Technology and Usage Data.

Client Delay means a failure or delay by the Client, an Authorized User or a person engaged by the Client, to perform an obligation or to provide information, access, credentials, Client Data, Client Content, decisions, feedback, Acceptance or payment by the time required under the Agreement or these Terms.
Client Portal means the online portal operated by Zatics Intelligence through which Project information, documents, approvals and communications are made available to the Client.

Configured Scope means the objectives, permissions, tools, data sources, integrations, thresholds, rules and limits that define what an AI System is configured to do, as set out in the Approved Blueprint, the Agreement or the Documentation.
Confidential Information has the meaning given in Section 22.
Custom Solution means a System or Deliverable designed and built by Zatics Intelligence for the Client under an Approved Blueprint.

Customization Work means work, other than the original Scope of a Custom Solution, that adds to or modifies an Existing Zatics Solution or a Custom Solution and that is approved under Section 4.5 or Section 9.
Data Protection Law means Applicable Law governing the processing of Personal Data.
Deliverable means an item, System, Software, Documentation, report or other work product that Zatics Intelligence is required to deliver to the Client under the Approved Blueprint or the Agreement.
Documentation means the user, technical and administrative guides, in any form, that Zatics Intelligence supplies for a System.
Effective Date means the date on which the Agreement takes effect as stated in it or, if no date is stated, the date of the last signature or approval.

Existing Zatics Solution means a software product, AI Agent, portal, automation system, module or other solution that was developed by or for Zatics Intelligence and is made available to clients under a License, other than a Custom Solution.

Fees means all amounts payable by the Client under the Agreement and these Terms, including project fees, upfront fees, milestone payments, license fees, subscription fees, customization fees, infrastructure fees, usage fees and support fees.
Force Majeure Event has the meaning given in Section 37.5.
License means a right to use Software or a System granted to the Client under Section 18 or Section 17.
Milestone means a defined stage, event or set of Deliverables identified in the Approved Blueprint or the Agreement, with an associated target date and, where applicable, an associated payment.
Output means text, code, images, data, predictions, classifications, recommendations, decisions, actions or other content generated by an AI System.
Personal Data means information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, as defined in Data Protection Law.
Production Release means the first making available of a Deliverable or System for live operational use by the Client.

Project means the engagement under which Zatics Intelligence designs, builds, configures, integrates or delivers a Custom Solution or performs Customization Work, as described in the Approved Blueprint.
Proposal means the written proposal, estimate or quotation prepared by Zatics Intelligence before approval of the Blueprint.
Review Period means the period, determined under Section 13, within which the Client may review and test a Deliverable.
Scope means the full set of work, Deliverables, features, integrations, workflows and responsibilities included in a Project, as defined in the Approved Blueprint and amended by any Change Order.
Security Incident means a confirmed unauthorized access to, or unauthorized acquisition, disclosure, loss or alteration of, Client Data in the possession or control of Zatics Intelligence.

Services means all services supplied by Zatics Intelligence under an Agreement, including discovery, consulting, design, development, configuration, integration, implementation, deployment, training, support, maintenance and access to hosted Systems.
Software means computer programs and code in any form, including source code, object code, scripts, interfaces, modules, model configurations and AI Agents, together with related updates.
Subscription Term means the period for which a License to an Existing Zatics Solution is granted under the Agreement, including any renewal period.

System means an integrated combination of Software, configurations, workflows, AI Systems, interfaces, infrastructure components and Documentation that is supplied or operated by Zatics Intelligence as part of the Services.
Terms Effective Date means the date on which this version of these Terms takes effect, as shown on the title page and in Section 39.

Third Party Components means software, libraries, models or other materials owned by a person other than Zatics Intelligence or the Client, including open source software, that are incorporated into or supplied with a Deliverable.

Third Party Services means products, services, platforms, models, APIs, infrastructure, software or data supplied by a person other than Zatics Intelligence or the Client and used in connection with the Services, including AI model providers, cloud infrastructure providers, communication platforms and payment providers.
Transferred Deliverable has the meaning given in Section 17.

Usage Data means technical and operational information about the performance, availability, usage and security of Systems that does not identify the Client or any individual and does not contain the substance of Client Data.
Warranty Period has the meaning given in Section 28.

Zatics Delay means a delay in meeting a Milestone date or delivery date that is caused by a failure of Zatics Intelligence to perform an obligation under the Agreement when due, and excludes any delay that is a Client Delay, a delay caused by Third Party Services, or a delay caused by a Force Majeure Event.
Zatics Intelligence means the business operating as Zatics Intelligence in India, with contact details set out in Section 38.

Zatics Technology means all Software, AI Systems, model configurations, frameworks, orchestration methods, tools, templates, libraries, algorithms, designs, processes, know-how and Documentation, whether existing before or developed independently of or in the course of the Services, together with all improvements and derivatives of them and all intellectual property rights in them, excluding Client Data, Client Content and any Transferred Deliverable.
Interpretation

Headings are for convenience and do not affect interpretation. The word including means including without limitation. A reference to days means calendar days unless Business Days are specified. A reference to writing includes email and a message delivered through the Client Portal. References to Sections are to Sections of these Terms unless stated otherwise.
ABOUT ZATICS INTELLIGENCE
Nature of the Business

Zatics Intelligence is a business to business technology company. It designs, builds, deploys and supports software systems, AI Systems and automation for organizations, and it licenses existing software products and AI Agents that it has developed.
Zatics Intelligence supplies its Services through two commercial models, Custom Solutions and Existing Zatics Solutions, which are described in Section 4.
Categories of Services
Depending on the Agreement, Zatics Intelligence may supply the following categories of Services:
(a)	custom software development, being the design and construction of software to a requirement approved by the Client;
(b)	AI Systems, being Systems that use machine learning or generative models to produce Outputs;
(c)	AI Agents, being AI Systems configured to perform tasks or invoke tools within a Configured Scope;
(d)	Autonomous Systems, being Systems that execute tasks and workflows without instruction at each step;
(e)	business automation, being the automation of defined business processes and workflows;
(f)	enterprise software, being software for the operation and management of an organization;
(g)	AI infrastructure, being the technical environment, tooling and integrations that support the operation of AI Systems;
(h)	system integrations, being the connection of Systems with the Client's systems and Third Party Services;
(i)	implementation, being configuration, deployment and onboarding of a System in the Client's environment;
(j)	consulting, being technical analysis, assessment and advice on systems, architecture and automation; and
(k)	support and maintenance, being the operation, correction and updating of Systems after delivery.
Basis on Which Services Are Supplied

Zatics Intelligence supplies only the Services described in the Agreement. The Services do not include legal, regulatory, financial, tax, accounting or medical advice, and Zatics Intelligence is not engaged as an adviser on those matters.

Zatics Intelligence may perform the Services remotely and from more than one location, and may engage subcontractors and Third Party Services in accordance with Section 24. Zatics Intelligence remains responsible to the Client for the performance of its subcontractors under the Agreement.
COMMERCIAL MODELS
Custom Built Solutions

A Custom Solution is built for a client in response to a specific business or technical requirement. Zatics Intelligence analyzes the requirement, prepares a Proposal and a Blueprint, and builds the System according to the Approved Blueprint.

Once the Client approves the final Blueprint under Section 6, the Approved Blueprint is the baseline for the Scope, the Deliverables, the timeline and the commercial terms of the Project. Fees for a Custom Solution are set out in the Approved Blueprint or the Agreement and are payable as described in Section 14.
Rights in a Custom Solution are governed by Section 17.
Existing Zatics Solutions

An Existing Zatics Solution is a product, AI Agent, portal, automation system, module or other solution that Zatics Intelligence has already developed. A client may obtain a License to an Existing Zatics Solution for a Subscription Term.

An Existing Zatics Solution is supplied in the form described in its Documentation and the Agreement. It is not built to the Client's individual requirement, and the Client does not acquire ownership of it by virtue of the License.
Software Licensing

A License permits the Client to use the Software or System for the Subscription Term, within the permitted users, limits and purposes stated in the Agreement and Section 18. A License does not transfer ownership of the Software, the System or any Zatics Technology.
The License fee, the Subscription Term, the number of Authorized Users and any usage limits are stated in the Agreement.
Purchase and Ownership Arrangements

Where Zatics Intelligence offers to sell or transfer ownership rights in a System, the Client may acquire those rights only under an Agreement that expressly defines the rights to be transferred, the purchase price, the payment schedule and the conditions of transfer.

Ownership does not transfer until the Client has satisfied every payment and transfer condition stated in the Agreement and in Section 17. A purchase arrangement does not transfer Zatics Technology unless the Agreement expressly identifies the Zatics Technology that is to be transferred.
Customization of Existing Solutions

A client who licenses an Existing Zatics Solution may request additional customizations, features, integrations, workflows, AI Agents or modifications. Work of this kind is additional Scope. It is not included in the License fee unless the Agreement states that it is.

Customization Work is requested, assessed and approved through the Change Request process in Section 9. It may be subject to separate development fees, infrastructure fees, usage fees or customization fees, and it may affect the timeline. Customization Work is performed only after the Client has approved a Change Order and satisfied any payment that the Change Order requires.

Unless the Change Order expressly provides otherwise, Customization Work forms part of the Existing Zatics Solution, is owned by Zatics Intelligence, and is licensed to the Client for the Subscription Term.

blocks.text: PROJECT DISCOVERY AND PROPOSAL
Initial Consultation and Requirement Gathering

The Project begins with an initial consultation in which Zatics Intelligence and the Client discuss the Client's objectives and requirements. Zatics Intelligence may then conduct a requirement gathering process, which may include workshops, interviews, document review and access to the Client's existing systems.

The Client is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of the information it provides during discovery. Zatics Intelligence relies on that information in preparing its assessment, Proposal and Blueprint.
Discovery work may be chargeable. Where discovery is chargeable, the Agreement or the Proposal will state the fee before the work begins.
Technical Assessment and Feasibility

Zatics Intelligence may carry out a technical assessment of the requirement, including a review of the Client's systems, data, integrations and constraints, and may assess the feasibility of the requirement.

A feasibility assessment reflects the information available at the time it is made. It is not a guarantee that a requirement can be met. Zatics Intelligence may revise its assessment if new information, a Third Party Service limitation or a technical constraint becomes apparent.
Proposal

Following discovery, Zatics Intelligence will prepare a Proposal. The Proposal will describe the proposed Services at a summary level and will include an estimated cost, an estimated timeline, the assumptions on which they are based and the exclusions that apply.
The Proposal is not the final statement of Scope. The final statement of Scope is the Approved Blueprint.
Estimated Cost and Estimated Timeline

Unless the Proposal expressly states a fixed price or a fixed date, the estimated cost and the estimated timeline are estimates prepared in good faith on the basis of the information and assumptions available at the time. They may be adjusted in the Blueprint.
When the Client approves the Blueprint, the project price and the timeline stated in the Approved Blueprint replace the estimates in the Proposal.
Assumptions and Exclusions

The Proposal and the Blueprint will record the assumptions on which they are based. Assumptions may concern the availability and quality of Client Data, the availability of Client personnel, the readiness of the Client's environment, the availability and terms of Third Party Services, and the absence of unusual regulatory requirements. If an assumption proves to be incorrect, Zatics Intelligence may submit a Change Request under Section 9 to address the effect on Scope, Fees or timeline.
Unless the Agreement or the Approved Blueprint states otherwise, the following are excluded from the Scope:
(a)	fees charged by Third Party Services, including AI model usage, cloud infrastructure and licenses of third party software;
(b)	hosting, infrastructure and operating costs after Production Release;
(c)	migration, cleansing or correction of Client Data;
(d)	changes to the Client's own systems or to systems operated by the Client's other suppliers;
(e)	training, support and maintenance beyond what the Agreement describes;
(f)	regulatory certification, audit or approval of a System; and
(g)	any feature, integration or workflow not described in the Approved Blueprint.
PROJECT BLUEPRINT
Purpose and Status of the Blueprint

The Blueprint is the central project document for a Custom Solution. Its purpose is to record, in a form that both parties can review and approve, what Zatics Intelligence will build, how it will be built, what the Client must provide, how completion will be measured, and what the Client will pay.

Once the final Blueprint is approved by the Client under this Section 6, the Approved Blueprint becomes the baseline for determining the agreed Scope, Deliverables, timeline and project price of the Project.
Contents of the Blueprint
Unless the Agreement provides otherwise, a Blueprint will address each of the following, to a level of detail appropriate to the Project:
(a)	the purpose and business objectives of the Project;
(b)	functional requirements, describing what the System is required to do;
(c)	technical requirements, including architecture, environments, performance expectations and constraints;
(d)	features, described individually where they are intended to form part of the Scope;
(e)	integrations with the Client's systems and with Third Party Services;
(f)	AI Agents, including their intended function and Configured Scope;
(g)	workflows and automation, including the points at which human review or approval is required;
(h)	Deliverables, including Documentation, training and handover items;
(i)	Milestones, with target dates and any associated payments;
(j)	dependencies, including those on the Client, on Third Party Services and on other parties;
(k)	Client responsibilities, as further described in Section 12;
(l)	Acceptance Criteria for each Deliverable or Milestone;
(m)	the project timeline;
(n)	the project price and payment schedule; and
(o)	the assumptions and exclusions that apply to the Project.
Preparation and Review
Zatics Intelligence will prepare the Blueprint on the basis of the information provided during discovery and will submit it to the Client through the Client Portal or by another written means.

The Client will review the Blueprint and, within ten (10) Business Days of its submission, will either approve it or provide consolidated written feedback identifying each requested correction. Zatics Intelligence will consider the feedback and submit a revised Blueprint. The Client will review each revised version within five (5) Business Days.

A requested change to a Blueprint that increases the Scope beyond the requirement described during discovery may result in an adjustment to the estimated cost and timeline before the Blueprint is approved.
Blueprint Approval

The Blueprint is approved when an authorized representative of the Client approves the identified version through the Client Portal, by signature, or by another method permitted under Section 35. Approval of a Blueprint is a binding commitment by the Client to the Scope, the Acceptance Criteria, the timeline and the project price stated in it.
Zatics Intelligence is not required to begin development until the Blueprint has been approved and any Upfront Fee that the Agreement makes a condition of commencement has been paid.

If the Client neither approves a Blueprint nor provides feedback within the periods in Section 6.3, Zatics Intelligence may issue a reminder. If the Client does not respond within five (5) Business Days of the reminder, Zatics Intelligence may treat the Project as paused under Section 10.6 and the Blueprint will not be treated as approved.
Baseline Effect of the Approved Blueprint

The Approved Blueprint is the sole authoritative statement of the Scope. A requirement, feature, integration, workflow or Deliverable that is not described in the Approved Blueprint is outside the Scope, even if it was mentioned in discussion or correspondence.

Where the Approved Blueprint is silent or ambiguous on a point of detail, Zatics Intelligence will resolve the point by reasonable technical judgment that is consistent with the stated purpose of the relevant Deliverable and does not materially increase the effort required. If resolving the point in the Client's preferred manner would materially increase effort, cost or time, the matter will be handled as a Change Request under Section 9.
Blueprint Versions

The Approved Blueprint may be changed only by a Change Order under Section 9, or by a correction of an evident clerical error that both parties confirm through the Client Portal and that does not alter the Scope, the Fees or the timeline.
Each version of a Blueprint is identified by a version number and a timestamp in the Client Portal. The version identified in the record of approval is the version that the Client has approved.
SCOPE CONTROL
Scope Definition

The Scope of a Project is the work and Deliverables described in the Approved Blueprint, as amended by any Change Order. The Scope of a License is the Software, System and functionality described in the Agreement and the Documentation.
Zatics Intelligence is responsible for performing the Scope. Zatics Intelligence is not required to perform, and the Fees do not include, work outside the Scope.
Included Work and Excluded Work
Included work is the work that is necessary to produce the Deliverables described in the Approved Blueprint in accordance with the Acceptance Criteria.

Excluded work includes any work that is not described in the Approved Blueprint, any matter identified as an exclusion in the Proposal, the Blueprint or the Agreement, and any matter listed in Section 5.5 unless the Approved Blueprint includes it.
Scope Freeze
On approval of the Blueprint, the Scope is frozen. After the Scope has been frozen, a change to the Scope may be made only through the Change Request process in Section 9.
Requirement Changes and Scope Clarification

The parties recognize that detailed implementation questions arise during a Project. A clarification of how an Approved Blueprint requirement is to be implemented is not a change to the Scope if it does not materially affect effort, cost, timeline, architecture or dependencies, as reasonably determined by Zatics Intelligence acting in good faith and recorded in the Client Portal. Zatics Intelligence will record each such clarification in the Client Portal.

A request that adds to, replaces or removes a feature, Deliverable, integration or workflow, or that changes a requirement stated in the Approved Blueprint, is a Change Request. A request that is not a Major Scope Change may be accepted by Zatics Intelligence without charge if Zatics Intelligence confirms in writing that it will do so. Absent that confirmation, it is handled under Section 9.
Client Responsibilities for Scope

The Client will nominate a single authorized representative who is responsible for communicating the Client's requirements and decisions. The Client will ensure that requirements and decisions given to Zatics Intelligence are consolidated, internally agreed and consistent with the Approved Blueprint. Zatics Intelligence is entitled to rely on instructions from the Client's authorized representative.
MAJOR SCOPE CHANGES
Definition of Major Scope Change

A Major Scope Change is a change to the Scope that, in the reasonable judgment of Zatics Intelligence, materially affects the architecture, the effort, the cost, the timeline or the dependencies of the Project. A Major Scope Change is a Change Request that always requires a Change Order.
Examples
The following are examples of Major Scope Changes:
(a)	replacing a major part of the approved architecture;
(b)	rebuilding components that have been substantially completed;
(c)	adding a major System or module;
(d)	adding a new platform, such as an additional web, mobile or desktop platform;
(e)	adding a major integration with a Client system or a Third Party Service;
(f)	adding a new AI Agent or materially changing the Configured Scope of an approved AI Agent;
(g)	changing a core workflow; and
(h)	changing a fundamental business requirement on which the Approved Blueprint is based.
Consequences of a Major Scope Change

A Major Scope Change may require additional Fees, an adjustment to Milestone dates and the final delivery date, a revision of the Approved Blueprint, a change to the resourcing of the Project and changes to infrastructure or usage Fees. Zatics Intelligence will describe these consequences in the Change Order proposal under Section 9.

Work performed to Acceptance Criteria that is rendered redundant or must be redone because of a Major Scope Change requested by the Client is chargeable at the rates stated in the Agreement or, if none are stated, at Zatics Intelligence's then-current rates, as described in the Change Order.
Determination

Zatics Intelligence will classify a Change Request as a Major Scope Change or not, and will state the reasons for its classification in writing. If the Client disagrees with the classification, the Client may raise a dispute under Section 36. The Change Request will remain unimplemented until the classification is resolved.
CHANGE REQUEST PROCESS
Formal Process
Every change to the Scope will be processed through the formal Change Request process in this Section 9. A Major Scope Change must not be implemented informally.
Stages of the Process
The Change Request process comprises the following stages:
(a)	the Client submits a Change Request in writing, describing the requested change, its purpose and the desired timing;
(b)	Zatics Intelligence evaluates the request and may ask the Client for further information;
(c)	Zatics Intelligence assesses the technical impact of the request on the Approved Blueprint, the System and the other Deliverables;
(d)	Zatics Intelligence assesses the cost of the request, including any additional development, infrastructure, usage or third party Fees;
(e)	Zatics Intelligence assesses the effect of the request on the timeline;
(f)	Zatics Intelligence issues a written Change Order proposal that sets out the results of those assessments;
(g)	the Client approves or declines the Change Order proposal;
(h)	where the Change Order requires an additional payment, the Client pays the amount that the Change Order specifies as a condition of commencement;
(i)	Zatics Intelligence begins the work described in the Change Order; and
(j)	Zatics Intelligence updates the Approved Blueprint or the project documentation to reflect the change.
Evaluation and Change Order Proposal

Zatics Intelligence will respond to a Change Request within ten (10) Business Days of receiving it, by issuing a Change Order proposal, by stating that it cannot accommodate the request, or by stating the additional time it needs to complete its assessment and the reason. Where the assessment is itself substantial, Zatics Intelligence may charge for it on the basis stated in advance.

A Change Order proposal remains open for approval for fifteen (15) Business Days from its date of issue unless it states a different period. After that period the proposal lapses and the assessment may need to be repeated.
Approval and Implementation

A Change Order takes effect when it has been approved by an authorized representative of each party. Zatics Intelligence will begin the work described in a Change Order after it has taken effect and any payment required as a condition of commencement has been received.
The Change Order prevails over earlier documents as provided in Section 1.7, and the Approved Blueprint is deemed amended to the extent stated in it.
No Informal Changes

A request made in conversation, in a call, in an informal message or in a comment on a Deliverable is not a Change Request and does not amend the Scope. Personnel of Zatics Intelligence have no authority to agree a change to the Scope, the Fees or the timeline other than through a Change Order.

If the Client instructs Zatics Intelligence in writing to begin work that is outside the Scope before a Change Order has taken effect, and Zatics Intelligence agrees to do so, the work is chargeable at the rates stated in the Agreement or, if none are stated, at Zatics Intelligence's then-current rates. Doing that work does not amend the Scope and does not waive any right of Zatics Intelligence under this Section 9.
Work Pending a Change Order

While a Change Request is under assessment or awaiting approval, Zatics Intelligence may continue the work that the Change Request does not affect. Zatics Intelligence may pause work on components that the Change Request affects, and any resulting delay is a Client Delay for the purposes of Section 10 to the extent that it arises from the pending Change Request.
PROJECT TIMELINE AND DELIVERY
Estimated Timelines and Milestones

The timeline in the Approved Blueprint is an estimate of the dates on which Milestones are expected to be reached and Deliverables are expected to be delivered. It is based on the assumptions in the Approved Blueprint, including the timely performance by the Client of its responsibilities.
A Milestone date or delivery date is a firm commitment only if the Agreement expressly describes it as a fixed date and states the remedy for failure to meet it.
Development Periods
